title: European sovereign routing workflow and tenant-level allow/deny enforcement
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Goal: implement a tenant-scoped European sovereignty mode that enforces routing of customer requests and persisted data to EU-only capacity, supports tenant allowlist/denylist controls, and defines deterministic fallback semantics when EU capacity or compatible model variants are unavailable. This ticket covers API surface, policy evaluation order, enforcement modes, telemetry, and a phased rollout plan for both hosted and Dedicated customers.
implementation_notes: Add new tenant flag: 'eu_sovereignty_mode' with values: off, soft_block, hard_block.
Policy evaluation order: 1) Tenant explicit denylist -> 2) Tenant allowlist -> 3) Region policy -> 4) Global fallback.
Routing decision uses tenant metadata + request attributes (region_hint, model_family, tier) and returns an enforcement reason code for telemetry.
Introduce 'fallback_type' enum in router: 'regional_variant', 'lower_tier_local', 'cross-region-escalation'. Only 'regional_variant' is allowed for hard_block tenants.
Persist routing decision in request trace header for post-hoc audits and ability to replay requests into matched region for debugging.
Update admission controller to validate that persisted objects (KV cache snapshots, logs) in customer workspace only target EU storage for hard_block tenants.
Plan a canary rollout: start with soft_block for internal tenants, run chaos test that simulates EU capacity exhaustion and validate fallback behavior.
Backward compatibility: default mode remains off; existing tenants must opt-in. Provide migration script to mark tenants with EU billing/contact as recommended opt-in candidates.
acceptance_criteria: API: Tenant config endpoint accepts eu_sovereignty_mode and allowlist/denylist arrays and returns current effective policy.
Routing: Requests from tenants in hard_block mode never route to non-EU compute; attempts are rejected with a clear error and audit entry.
Fallback: For soft_block tenants, router selects a region-local compatible model variant when EU variant capacity is exhausted and logs a fallback_reason in tracing.
Telemetry: We emit 'routing.decision' counter with tags {tenant, mode, enforcement, fallback_type, target_region} and a dashboard with trend and P99 latency by routing outcome.
E2E tests: Integration test that simulates EU-only capacity reached and verifies both soft_block fallback selection and hard_block rejection.
Security: KMS/keys and storage paths for hard_block tenants are validated by admission controller and verified by security review.
Docs & UX: Console shows tenant EU sovereignty state, allowlist/denylist editor, and an explanation of fallback semantics; docs updated with migration steps.
Rollout: Canary on 10 internal tenants for 2 weeks with runbook and automatic rollback criteria defined.
qa_steps: Create tenant in soft_block mode + add allowlist entry, send requests with region_hint=eu -> assert routing to eu variant and logs show enforcement=soft.
Force EU variant downtime in staging -> assert soft_block tenant falls back to regional_variant and fallback_type recorded.
Create tenant in hard_block and attempt to route to us-west -> expect 403-like rejection and audit log entry referencing policy id.
Check that persisted KV snapshots for hard_block tenants are written only to EU storage endpoints in staging.
Run automated meltdown test: spike 10k requests and verify routing decisions remain under 250ms and no silent cross-region routing for hard_block tenants.
Validate console UI: toggling mode and editing allowlist persists and reads back correctly via API.
risks: Incorrect policy precedence could lead to unintended cross-region routing for regulated tenants -> high severity.
Telemetry gaps could make post-incident audits difficult; ensure routing.decision tag coverage before rollout.
Performance regression: extra policy checks on hot path may add latency; optimize policy cache and precompute effective policy for tenant.
Operational complexity for Dedicated customers with mixed-region pools; migration may require coordination with infra ops.
Legal interpretation edge-cases for 'EU residency' (e.g., Norway/Switzerland) require legal sign-off on region definitions.
